source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. Stories and worked quantities are originally authored constructed examples, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate evidence before publication.
purpose: Compare a selected sample with the whole population and see how one changed value affects each mean.
meaning: A population is the complete collection under study, while a sample is a selected part of that collection. An arithmetic mean summarizes its own values. The live example keeps the full population visible so that a chosen sample statistic can be compared with the population parameter and its signed difference.

definition.setting: Descriptive statistics for a known finite population of twelve distinctly labeled crate weights. Selection is a deliberate cyclic window, not a random experiment.

signature.x: Mass of the changing last crate, from 0 to 30 kilograms.
signature.n: Integer number of selected crates in [1,12].
signature.s: Number of crates skipped before selection, an integer from 0 to 11.
signature.∑xᵢ: Sum of the n selected crate weights.
signature.∑Xᵢ: Sum of all twelve crate weights.
signature.E: Sample mean minus population mean, in kilograms.

conditions: The finite population is twelve labeled crate masses in kilograms: [8, 9, 9, 10, 10, 10, 11, 11, 12, 12, 13, x]. Different crates remain distinct even when their masses match.
The last crate has mass x, with 0 ≤ x ≤ 30 kg. Only x changes; the other eleven masses stay fixed.

Sample size n is an integer from 1 to 12. Skip s crates (an integer from 0 to 11), then select n consecutive crates. Continue from crate 1 after crate 12 (wraparound), without selecting a crate twice.
The selected mean is x̄ = (∑xᵢ)/n. The population mean is μ = (∑Xᵢ)/12. Both means are measured in kilograms; totals and counts are different quantities.
The mean difference is E = x̄ − μ. A positive E means the selected crates have the higher average mass.
This deliberately chosen contiguous window is not a simple random sample. No randomization, unbiased-estimator guarantee, confidence interval or sampling distribution is produced.
A census uses all twelve distinct crate labels and makes the sample mean equal to this known finite-population mean.
If the highlighted crate is outside the selected sample, changing it leaves the sample mean fixed while changing the population mean.
definition.domain_notes: The broader subject distinguishes descriptive summaries from statistical inference. This specimen has a known finite population and deterministic sample selection. It does not simulate random sampling, infer an unknown population mean, produce a confidence level, or implement sample variance. The ordering of the labeled crates does not imply that observations are independent random draws.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level references; restricted-family properties are author-derived. Independent mathematical review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: N = 12; ∑Xᵢ = 115 + x; μ = (115 + x)/12. Skip s crates and select n consecutive crates, continuing from crate 1 after crate 12. Then x̄ = (∑xᵢ)/n and E = x̄ − μ.
grammar.precedence: Choose the distinct crate labels first, add their weights once each, and divide by their positive count. Compute the full-population sum separately before comparing the two means.

prompts.prompt: Does a larger chosen sample automatically become random?
prompts.answer: No. Sample size and selection method are separate. This cyclic rule is deterministic at every size.

prompts.prompt: Why keep repeated weights as separate bars?
prompts.answer: The population contains labeled crates. Two crates with the same weight are still two observations and both contribute to the mean.

representations.description: A bar for every population observation, selected sample labels and two separate arithmetic-mean reference lines connect membership to sample and population sums.
Sample mean and population mean are plotted against the highlighted last value while sample size and starting index stay fixed. An excluded highlighted value gives a flat sample-mean curve.
Selected sample sum divided by sample size and full population sum divided by N remain separate, followed by the signed mean difference.
